title: melgarafael/DeskcommCRM
abstract:
🇧🇷 Português · 🇺🇸 English · 🇪🇸 Español 🛠️ DeskcommCRM — o Sistema Operacional de Vendas com IA, open source, pro WhatsApp Agentes de IA que atendem, qualificam e vendem no WhatsApp — dentro de um CRM open source rodando no seu servidor. Sem mensalidade, sem feature travada, seus dados com você. A alternativa aberta a Kommo, Octadesk e Intercom. ⚡ Instalar · 📖 Curso visual · 🔄 Atualizar · 🧭 Visão · 🏗️ Arquitetura · 🤝 Contribuir · 🗺️ Roadmap ☁️ Rode este CRM em produção com 1 comando O DeskcommCRM foi desenvolvido em parceria com a HostGator : o hostgator-setup-kit/ instala o CRM completo (app + WhatsApp + banco) numa VPS com um único comando, e o runbook de produção já assume esse ambiente. 👉 Assinar a VPS HostGator com desconto da parceria —
datacenter em São Paulo, ideal pro WhatsApp rodando 24/7. (link de parceiro — assinar por ele apoia o projeto e sai mais barato) Ainda não tem servidor? Rode isto no seu computador (macOS, Linux ou WSL). Ele diz
qual plano contratar — com os números do runbook, não um "depende" — e te devolve o
comando certo pro seu caso: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/melgarafael/DeskcommCRM/main/hostgator-setup-kit/comecar.sh | bash (prefere ler antes de executar? clone o repo e rode bash hostgator-setup-kit/comecar.sh —
ele não instala nada sem você confirmar.) ⚡ Instalar na sua VPS (o caminho principal) 1. Entre na sua VPS Abra o Terminal no seu computador (no Windows, o PowerShell ; no Mac ou Linux, o Terminal ) e conecte com o IP e a porta que a hospedagem te mandou por e-mail: ssh -p PORTA root@SEU_IP Troque PORTA e SEU_IP pelos seus. Se a hospedagem não mencionou porta nenhuma, é a padrão
(22) e você pode omitir: ssh root@SEU_IP . Ele pede a senha. Ao digitar, não aparece nada na tela — nem asteriscos. Isso não é
travamento: é o terminal escondendo a senha. Digite (ou cole) e dê Enter. Na primeira conexão ele pergunta Are you sure you want to continue connecting? — responda yes . É o servidor se apresentando pela primeira vez. 2. Rode o instalador Já dentro da VPS: git clone https://github.com/melgarafael/DeskcommCRM.git cd DeskcommCRM
bash hostgator-setup-kit/install.sh É isso. Você não instala Node, nem pnpm, nem compila nada — a imagem do app já vem pronta.
Se faltar Docker, o instalador pergunta e instala sozinho. O que você precisa ter em mãos Item Onde conseguir VPS com Docker HostGator (parceria) — ou qualquer VPS com Docker. 4 GB de RAM recomendados Domínio Um registro A apontando pro IP da VPS (ex.: crm.suaempresa.com.br ) Banco Conta grátis no supabase.com — 3 chaves + connection string do Session pooler . Se o projeto ficar fora do ar parado ( 522 ou PGRST002 por horas), o compute Nano do plano grátis pode não bastar: veja o runbook IA Uma chave de OpenRouter , Anthropic ou OpenAI — o instalador pergunta qual você quer WhatsApp Seu número, conectado por QR code no onboarding (ou o canal oficial da Meta) O instalador também atende VPS ARM64/aarch64, como a Oracle Ampere A1, e escolhe a imagem
NOWEB oficial do WAHA compatível com essa arquitetura. Vale para os dois caminhos: com Supabase
externo e com o Supabase na mesma VPS (as imagens do Supabase self-hosted fixadas pelo kit também
são publicadas para linux/arm64 ). Nada é compilado na VPS. 💡 O Supabase pode ser criado pelo próprio instalador. Exporte um SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN antes de rodar e ele cria o projeto, espera o banco ficar saudável,
busca as 4 credenciais e descobre o host do pooler testando conexão real — sem copiar e colar. O que o instalador faz por você Ele pergunta só o que é seu (domínio, chaves, senha do admin), valida cada resposta antes
de seguir — chave errada ele recusa na hora, não três passos depois — e cuida do resto: Gera todos os segredos técnicos sozinho (você não inventa senha nenhuma). Cria as extensões do Postgres e aplica o schema completo ( supabase/baseline.sql ). Cria o primeiro admin com o e-mail e a senha que você escolheu. Sobe a stack inteira com HTTPS automático e confere a saúde no fim. Instala o cron das automações (sem ele, as regras QUANDO/SE/ENTÃO ficam paradas na fila)
e o agente de atualização , que é o que faz o botão "Atualizar agora" existir na tela. Rodar de novo não quebra nada — o install.sh é idempotente: não duplica cron, não recria
usuário, retoma de onde parou. Modo não-interativo: copie .env.hostgator.example para .env , preencha e rode bash hostgator-setup-kit/install.sh --yes . Outra hospedagem? (Hostinger, Coolify, Dokploy, CapRover…) Funciona. Se a sua VPS já vem com um proxy reverso próprio ocupando as portas 80/443, o
instalador detecta isso sozinho e publica o CRM através dele, em vez de tentar subir um
Caddy que não caberia. Num caso específico — proxy em --network host , como faz a Hostinger —
ele pergunta em vez de adivinhar , porque publicar atrás do proxy errado instala "com
sucesso" um site mudo. Detalhes em hostgator-setup-kit/README.md . Primeiro acesso Abra https://<seu-domínio> (o cadeado leva ~1 min pra aparecer), entre com o admin, e tenha o Google Authenticator ou Authy à mão se você quiser ligar a verificação em duas etapas — ela é opcional e fica em Configurações › Segurança; o primeiro login não a exige. No onboarding,
escaneie o QR code com o WhatsApp do seu número. Já instalou? Continue no curso visual gratuito :
telas reais e indicações de onde clicar para aprender a usar a Inbox, organizar o funil e
configurar seus agentes de IA, no seu ritmo. 🤖 Prefere que uma IA instale pra você? O repositório traz guias do assistente que carregam sozinhos no Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
OpenCode ou Antigravity: instalar, montar um cliente por nicho, analisar métricas, afinar o prompt
do agente e contribuir. Para tê-los em qualquer pasta — inclusive antes de clonar, no seu
computador —, rode uma vez: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/melgarafael/DeskcommCRM/main/scripts/instalar-guias.sh | bash Depois abra uma sessão nova do seu assistente e diga "quero instalar o CRM na minha VPS" : pedir o
assunto em português aciona o guia certo em qualquer um dos cinco. Para chamar um guia pelo nome,
cada um tem o seu jeito — /deskcomm-instalar no Claude Code, no Cursor e no Antigravity; $deskcomm-instalar no Codex; no OpenCode, peça pelo nome, em linguagem natural. Os guias não se atualizam sozinhos: rodar o mesmo comando de novo traz a versão nova. Para
desfazer: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/melgarafael/DeskcommCRM/main/scripts/instalar-guias.sh | bash -s -- --remover Com o repositório já clonado, os guias vêm dentro dele ( .agents/skills/ ) e nem isso é preciso. Se
você rodou o comando mesmo assim, saiba que no Claude Code o guia instalado vale mais que o do clone
— e fica na versão do dia em que rodou, até rodar de novo (ou desfazer).
Também funciona o jeito antigo: jogar só a pasta hostgator-setup-kit/ no chat do Claude Code dentro da VPS — ele lê o CLAUDE.md do kit e conduz tudo em português. 🔄 Atualizar Saiu versão nova? Há dois caminhos, e o primeiro não exige terminal . Pela tela (recomendado) Quando existe versão nova, o rodapé do menu lateral acende "Nova versão" — só pro dono do
servidor, porque avisar quem não pode atualizar é ruído. Clique e você cai em Configurações → Atualização , que mostra o que muda, faz backup do banco sozinha e
acompanha cada fase (backup → código → banco → no ar) até terminar. Nada de SSH. Se a versão nova subir quebrada, o agente volta pra imagem anterior sozinho e grava essa
volta no .env — sem isso, o próximo restart traria o app quebrado de novo, em silêncio. Por baixo: o app só registra o pedido; quem executa é o agente que o install.sh deixou na
sua VPS, num cron que confere a cada 5 minutos — então a atualização começa em até 5
minutos depois do clique. Se esse agente estiver fora do ar, a tela avisa "Atualização automática indisponível" e mostra o comando abaixo — ela não finge que deu certo. Pelo terminal cd /caminho/do/DeskcommCRM
bash hostgator-setup-kit/update.

title: anomalyco/hex
abstract:
Hex Speak. It appears. Local-first voice dictation, built in Rust. Download for Mac, Windows, or Linux · Windows beta · Linux beta · TypeScript SDK · Contributing Hex is local-first voice dictation for Apple silicon Macs running macOS 15 or
newer. Hold a shortcut, speak, and release. Hex transcribes on your Mac and
pastes the result into the app you are using. On-device transcription. Download a local speech model during setup;
ordinary dictation does not require OpenCode or a cloud transcription service. Your words, your way. Choose a shortcut, language, and model. Use Modes for
corrections, application-specific behavior, and optional text processing. The macOS app is available now. The Windows beta covers x64 and
ARM64 PCs, and the Linux beta covers x86_64 X11 and compatible
wlroots Wayland compositors. See Privacy and local data for what stays on your device and what optional features send to a provider. Install Hex Downloads Stable is the current release. Dev is the newest build of dev , published
on every change; it updates itself from the Dev channel. Platform Stable Dev macOS (Apple silicon) DMG DMG Windows x64 Installer Installer Windows ARM64 Installer Installer Linux x86_64 Executable Executable Linux x86_64 (Debian, Ubuntu) .deb .deb Linux x86_64 (Fedora, openSUSE) .rpm .rpm Linux ARM64 Executable Executable Linux ARM64 (Debian, Ubuntu) .deb .deb Linux ARM64 (Fedora, openSUSE) .rpm .rpm macOS updater ZIP ZIP Windows x64 updater EXE EXE Windows ARM64 updater EXE EXE On Arch Linux you can also use yay -S hex-bin , or the install script below. With Homebrew: brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex Then launch Hex from Applications and complete setup. The cask installs the same signed app and keeps its built-in updater. Existing
DMG installations can keep using Check for Updates ; Homebrew does not migrate
or forcibly replace another app already named Hex.app . Or install manually: Download the signed DMG and open it. Drag Hex.app into Applications, then launch it. Complete the permission and model steps in setup. Microphone lets Hex record while you dictate. Accessibility lets Hex notice its shortcut in every app and paste into the foreground app. Drag the Hex tile into the list. Hex does not need Input Monitoring. Transcription model downloads the speech model that runs locally. Hex checks for signed updates automatically. Use Hex > Check for Updates… to check immediately. Organizations that manage app versions themselves can turn off in-app updates,
including manual checks, with the DisableUpdates Boolean in the anomaly.hex preference domain. Deploy it in a configuration profile
(payload type anomaly.hex , key DisableUpdates , value true ), or for a
single Mac run defaults write anomaly.hex DisableUpdates -bool true . On
Windows, set the DWORD DisableUpdates to 1 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Anomaly\Hex (Group Policy) or the same path in HKCU.
Relaunch Hex to apply it. Model downloads still work. Releases through 2.3.1
used the com.kitlangton.hex2 domain; profiles for those keep applying only to them. Download blocked? Each app release on GitHub Releases has the identical signed files. App releases use v… tags ( app-v… through
2.3.1); the repository also publishes separate TypeScript SDK releases.
If an older installation cannot check for updates on your network, install the
DMG manually over the existing Rust app. On managed networks, ask IT to allow anoma.ly : Hex downloads and updates
from the Anomaly release service at https://anoma.ly/release (releases up to
2.3.1 use https://anoma.ly/hex/files ). Local model setup separately needs huggingface.co and its model
download CDN. A successful
app download does not establish that those model hosts are reachable. After
restoring access, retry model preparation in Settings. Coming from the original Swift app? Install the new app manually and complete
setup. Settings and history are not transferred. Quit the old app before
dictating in the new one so their shortcuts do not compete. Dictate Anywhere Hold Option , speak, then release. Hex transcribes and pastes at the current
focus. Double-tap Option to keep recording; press Option again to finish. Press Escape to cancel. While recording, Escape discards the recording; after
you release, it cancels the newest dictation that is still transcribing, so
nothing is pasted for it. Press Option-Shift-V to paste the last completed dictation again. Settings let you change the shortcut, microphone, language, local model,
recording behavior, feedback volume, launch-at-login behavior, and Dock
visibility. Corrections in Modes fix names and preferred spellings before text
is pasted; modes can also apply optional rewriting and text transformations. Use menu bar > Transcription Model to switch between downloaded models without
opening Settings. Each model remembers its last selected language and, for
Whisper, recognition hints. Choose the language in Settings once, then switch
between combinations such as English with Parakeet and French with Whisper from
the menu. Manage Models… opens the full picker for downloads and language changes. Optional OpenCode Features OpenCode is optional, and ordinary dictation does not
require it. Hex never launches OpenCode: these features use an OpenCode service
that is already running, and say "OpenCode isn't running" otherwise. Post-processing: enable OpenCode in Modes to rewrite a transcript before
paste. Hex sends the transcript, foreground application, and Brave website
hostname to the configured model provider. Modes can target applications and
websites in Brave Browser. If OpenCode rewriting fails, Hex keeps the corrected local transcript and still
runs any selected text transformations. If that transformation stage fails, Hex
keeps the text from before the stage, not partial transformation results. Annotate Annotate records your screen while you draw on it and talk, then hands the
recording to an agent: its keyframes, your drawing, and a transcript of what
you said. It is on by default on macOS and Linux (Settings › Annotate; not on
Windows yet). Nothing is recorded, and no screen permission is asked for,
until you first use it. One key: Option-Shift-S on macOS, F9 on Linux. Tap it to start
and tap again to stop. While it records, hold it and move the pointer to
draw, no click needed; let go and the mouse is the app's again. macOS asks
for Screen Recording the first time; Linux asks through the desktop's
screen-sharing dialog once, then remembers the screen. While it records,
the dictation shortcut does nothing. The bar: the recording bar at the top shows the timer, a pen (click it,
then drag to draw like a real pen; click it again or press Esc to stop), stop, and ✕ to
discard. On macOS, holding Shift draws too. Ink fades from the screen
after about a second but stays in the recording. Paste or send: when it stops, the annotation is on your clipboard and
the capsule offers Paste (the contact sheet, then the summary) and Inspect . With OpenCode running, Send to… lists its sessions (macOS
also opens its suggestions by itself): click one to send it there, and Undo
takes it back for a few seconds. A send carries the transcript and the
pictures inline, so it works with an OpenCode server on another machine. hex annotate list|show|send (also hex capture … ) reads and sends from the
terminal. Custom Transformations Advanced users can create ~/.config/hex/hex.config.ts for deterministic
dictation transformations, written in TypeScript or JavaScript. Hex runs the
config itself in an embedded JavaScript engine and reloads it on save; nothing
else needs installing. hex commands init creates the starter workspace, and hex commands check reports what the config registers or why it fails. Config scripts get no filesystem, network, or process access.

title: openai/codex
abstract: Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer. If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE. If you want the desktop app experience, run codex app or visit the Codex App page . If you are looking for the cloud-based agent from OpenAI, Codex Web , go to chatgpt.com/codex . Quickstart Installing and running Codex CLI Run the following on Mac or Linux to install Codex CLI: curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh Run the following on Windows to install Codex CLI: powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c " irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex " The standalone installers download from https://releases.openai.com/codex by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable. To force GitHub Releases, set CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM to false ( 0 and no are also accepted): curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh $ env: CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM = ' false ' ; irm https: // chatgpt.com / codex / install.ps1 | iex Codex CLI can also be installed via the following package managers: # Install using npm npm install -g @openai/codex # Install using Homebrew brew install --cask codex Then simply run codex to get started. You can also go to the latest GitHub Release and download the appropriate binary for your platform. Each GitHub Release contains many executables, but in practice, you likely want one of these: macOS Apple Silicon/arm64: codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz x86_64 (older Mac hardware): codex-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz Linux x86_64: codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz arm64: codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl ), so you likely want to rename it to codex after extracting it. Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan Run codex and select Sign in with ChatGPT . We recommend signing into your ChatGPT account to use Codex as part of your Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan. Learn more about what's included in your ChatGPT plan . You can also use Codex with an API key, but this requires additional setup . Source-visible enterprise components are commercially licensed. anarlog The privacy-first AI meeting notepad. Open source, local-first, and yours to fork. Granola, rearranged. Website • Docs • Download • Discord • r/anarlog • @anarlogapp • Status anarlog is an open-source alternative to Granola. It takes notes in your meetings without sending a bot to join the call: it listens to your device audio, can transcribe on your machine, and keeps app data in a local SQLite database. It is built for people who want AI meeting notes without handing their conversations to someone else's cloud, and for anyone who needs to get a notetaker past a security review with a straight face. Why anarlog No bot joins your call. anarlog captures audio directly on your device. Nothing appears in the participant list, and nothing records from inside the meeting. Local when you choose it. On supported Macs, available built-in transcription models run on-device. Local Intelligence providers keep summaries and chat on your computer too. Your data, in a format you can read. Sessions, notes, and transcripts live in local SQLite. Recordings and attachments are plain local files. Export Markdown whenever it fits your workflow. Bring your own AI. Use a supported hosted provider, your own API key, or an OpenAI-compatible local server such as Ollama, LM Studio, or Unsloth. Readable source, MIT. The community application is MIT-licensed. Fork it, audit it, sell it, or build it yourself. Cloud is opt-in, not required. Hosted AI, encrypted CloudSync, and sharing exist when you want them. Nothing depends on them. A front door for your org. Source-visible enterprise components and commercial deployment options give security and IT teams a real path to yes. What runs where Part of the workflow Where it happens Audio capture and recording Your device Transcription Your device with an on-device model, or the provider you select Notes and transcript storage Local SQLite plus local files AI summaries and chat Your choice: local model, your own API key, or optional hosted AI Sync and sharing Off by default, opt-in encrypted CloudSync How AI works anarlog keeps audio transcription separate from the language model used for summaries and chat. You can change either one without changing the other. Stage App setting Anarlog Cloud Local or bring your own Audio → transcript Transcription Managed Pro (Cloud) prefers Soniox 5 for live and batch transcription, with eligible fallbacks based on language and mode. Soniqo or Apple Speech when available, or your selected transcription provider and model Transcript + memo → summary, title, or chat Intelligence Managed Auto (also shown as Pro (Cloud)) currently uses the latest Claude Sonnet alias through OpenRouter. Your selected API, subscription, OpenAI-compatible server, or eligible Apple Intelligence The active provider and model are always visible under Settings → Transcription and Settings → Intelligence . Read Models and providers for the current routes, local model list, and privacy boundaries. Get started Download Anarlog for macOS, Windows, or Linux. Open it and join a meeting. anarlog records on your device and transcribes with the model you selected. Generate a note, edit it like a document, and export Markdown when you need it. Optional: connect an LLM provider or a local model in settings for summaries and chat. Product docs live at docs.anarlog.so . To build the desktop app or website from source, follow Local development . Repository map Path What lives there apps/desktop Tauri v2 desktop app: React and TypeScript UI, Rust backend apps/web anarlog.so website, account portal, and shared-note pages; not the desktop notepad apps/api Optional hosted services for AI, sync, sharing, and integrations apps/cli Local CLI and MCP server apps/mobile iOS and Android client, available as a beta through TestFlight and Google Play apps/stripe Billing integration apps/watch/apple watchOS companion source built with the mobile app plugins/* Tauri capabilities such as local STT, database access, calendar, export, and notifications crates/* Rust libraries for audio capture, transcription, diarization, storage, and services packages/* Shared TypeScript packages for the editor, database, UI, and plugin SDK supabase/ Hosted authentication, sharing, sync, billing, and Cloud API data skills/anarlog Published agent skill for the CLI and MCP server enterprise/ Source-visible enterprise components, commercially licensed Local development The local-first desktop app and website start without secrets. Hosted AI, CloudSync, authentication, billing, and connected integrations need their optional local services and configuration. You need Node.js 22 or later, pnpm 11.1.1, Rust 1.94.0, process-compose 1.122.0 or later ( brew install process-compose on macOS), and the Tauri v2 system dependencies . Apple Silicon Macs also need Xcode with its Metal Toolchain component to compile the MLX shader library (Xcode 26 and later: DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain ); the Command Line Tools alone are not enough. On Debian or Ubuntu, the repository can install the required toolchains and system packages: bash scripts/setup-linux.sh Install the workspace and start the app you want to work on: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev:desktop # or pnpm dev:web Process Compose builds shared UI first, manages the app processes, and saves logs under .process-compose/ . Use pnpm dev for the combined desktop, web, API, and local Supabase stack after configuring the optional backend. Read CONTRIBUTING.md for backend setup, process controls, validation commands, code ownership, and the contribution workflow. Ask DeepWiki for a code-indexed explanation of a subsystem. Name history anarlog started as Hyprnote , then briefly used the char name. We later split the work into two projects. char is the team's current productivity app. anarlog is this open-source, local-first meeting notetaker. This repository is not the current char codebase, and anarlog is not being retired. Its community application stays MIT-licensed, forkable, buildable from source, and built for local notes you control. If you came here from Granola, welcome. If you came here from Hyprnote, welcome back. Either way, it's yours. Contributing Issues, pull requests, bug reports, and docs fixes are all welcome. Read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a pull request. Join the community on Discord or r/anarlog . Contributions outside enterprise/ are distributed under the MIT license. title: Nasiko-Labs/nasiko
abstract:
Nasiko is the OpenRuntime for agents, coding harnesses, frameworks and tools. Find the coding agents already running. See what each one costs, by harness and model. Route them to the models you choose while developers keep using their existing harness workflows. 📚 Documentation • 💬 Discord • 🐛 Report a bug Table of Contents What is Nasiko? Start here: see what is already running Coding agents: reporting and routing Features Why this runs in the call path Architecture Requirements Quick Start: Docker only (no Rust needed) Setup guides by operating system Deploying your own agents Environment Variables Project Structure Troubleshooting Project Activity Documentation & Links Support Contributing License What is Nasiko? Your developers are already running coding agents. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, often
more than one at a time, each with its own dashboard and its own billing unit. At the end of the
month there is a real bill, and nobody can say who spent it, on which model, or what it produced. Nasiko finds those agents, puts their spend in one schema, and hands back the model choice the
harness made for you. An OpenRuntime belongs to no vendor inside it: your cost history, your policy
and your model choice stay with you rather than with whichever harness you happened to install. Two properties hold the rest of this together, and they are not the same thing. Non-invasive discovery is about your architecture. Nasiko can detect the harnesses you already
run without changing their configuration. Reporting and routing are explicit opt-ins that add hooks
or update harness settings, but they require no wrapper or SDK in your application code. Non-intrusive operation is about your day. After one-time setup, developers keep using the same
harness commands and interfaces. OpenCode must be restarted after its plugin is installed, and
Codex asks you to trust the new Nasiko hooks. Nasiko Dashboard : deploy agents, route traffic, manage tools, and watch traces. Start here: see what is already running Install the current CLI from this checkout, then run its read-only discovery command: git clone https://github.com/Nasiko-Labs/nasiko.git && cd nasiko
cargo install --path cli/ --force
nasiko agents discover nasiko agents discover reads your machine, prints what it finds, and exits. You get a row per
supported harness: whether it is detected, whether it is reporting to Nasiko, its version, and
where its config lives. Discovery changes no harness settings, requires no account, and sends
nothing off the machine. If nasiko agents discover is not listed by nasiko agents --help , reinstall with the --force command above. Older builds use the same 0.1.0 version number, so nasiko --version alone cannot tell you whether the command is present. Harness Discovery and session reporting LLM routing Claude Code yes yes Codex yes yes OpenCode yes yes Cursor CLI yes not yet Those four are the supported set today and we will continue to add support for me. If you have a request please create an issue! The CLI is a Rust crate, so this path needs Rust . Reporting and routing also
need an active control plane and valid login: see Quick Start . Coding agents: reporting and routing Nasiko manages the coding-agent CLIs already installed on your machine: it can record what they
do, route their LLM calls, or both. The two are independent opt-ins. agents uninstall removes
local reporting hooks but preserves the registered agent and its history; disconnect restores
routing settings, though a running harness may need to be stopped or disconnected with --force . Session reporting nasiko agents discover # DETECTED / CONNECTED / VERSION / CONFIG per agent nasiko agents install < agent > # claude, codex, opencode, or cursor nasiko agents install < agent > --no-content # omit prompt and response text nasiko agents uninstall < agent > nasiko agents sync # flush queued session-turn events to the control plane Auto-install also fires on nasiko connect <control-plane-url> , nasiko use , and nasiko auth login , but only when authenticated and only for agents with no existing install
record . Routing commands such as nasiko connect claude do not trigger auto-install. Nasiko never
silently rebinds an already-installed agent to a new cluster; rebind explicitly with nasiko agents install <agent> . Nasiko installs each harness's supported event hooks: Claude uses Stop , OpenCode reports on session.idle , and Codex and Cursor use their richer hook event sets. Completed turns are queued
locally under ~/.nasiko/integrations/queue/ and delivered to POST /api/telemetry/coding-agent/events/batch , so a control plane that is briefly unreachable
costs you nothing. Permanently-failed deliveries (after a cluster is deleted or renamed, say) land
in ~/.nasiko/integrations/rejected/ and are safe to delete. Ingested turns show up as chat sessions right away ( nasiko sessions , nasiko history <id> ).
Traces, token counts, and cost additionally require CODING_AGENT_OTLP_ENDPOINT , covered below. Routing: give the harness back the model choice Some harnesses arrive tied to a provider by default. Claude Code defaults to Anthropic; Codex
defaults to OpenAI. That choice arrived with the tool rather than with you. Register a provider and key with Nasiko once, then point a harness at Nasiko instead of at its
vendor. Inbound wire protocol and outbound provider are decoupled, so an Anthropic-format request
from Claude Code is served by your OpenAI key: nasiko llm-config create --name my-openai --provider openai --model gpt-4o \
  --api-key-secret OPENAI_API_KEY --secret-value " $OPENAI_API_KEY " nasiko connect claude --config my-openai The full set of bindings: nasiko connect claude --config < llm-config-name > nasiko connect codex --config < llm-config-name > nasiko connect opencode --config < llm-config-name > nasiko disconnect < agent > # reverse the settings/plugin changes nasiko status < agent > # show current binding connect claude configures Claude Code's apiKeyHelper and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL . connect codex adds a model_providers.nasiko entry and command-based auth to Codex's config.toml . Their
credential helpers obtain a one-hour JWT from POST /api/agents/{id}/llm-token ; Codex refreshes
its credential on a timer rather than minting one for every request. Claude Code sends the
credential in the x-api-key header rather than Authorization ; the router accepts both. connect opencode instead installs plugins/nasiko-llm-router.js under OpenCode's config
directory (respecting OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR and XDG_CONFIG_HOME ), registers a nasiko provider,
and makes nasiko/router the default model for new OpenCode sessions only. OpenCode fixes a
session's model at creation time in its own database, so resuming an existing session will not
route it. Start a new one, or pick "Nasiko Router" explicitly. Inbound wire protocol and outbound provider are fully decoupled: nasiko connect claude --config my-openai-config routes Claude Code's Anthropic-format traffic to OpenAI. ~/.claude/settings.json and OpenCode's config are per-user, global files. Connecting an agent
affects every Claude Code / OpenCode process on the machine, not just the current project. LLM config management nasiko llm-config create --name < name > --provider < provider > --model < model > nasiko llm-config list
nasiko llm-config update < name > [--provider ...] [--model ...]
nasiko llm-config set-default < name > nasiko llm-config attach < name > --agent < agent > # attach to a deployed agent nasiko llm-config detach --agent < agent > nasiko llm-config get < agent > # resolved routing config for an agent nasiko llm-config providers # valid provider/model values + pricing Set a config's model for predictable routing. If it is unset, the router falls back through tier
models and then the platform default; list shows provider/? for the unset value. Server configuration Everything is env-driven. server/.env.

title: Proton's CEO Cancels AI 'Re-Interviews'
abstract:
On Friday, Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, cancelled a series of nearly company-wide ‘re-interviews’ that would have forced employees to explain how they are using AI, with the clear intention that they may be fired if not using it enough in the eyes of Proton leadership, according to six current Proton employees and audio of an around two hour all-hands meeting obtained by 404 Media. The move came after 404 Media published an investigation on Thursday, which showed how Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton, in some cases despite security concerns from employees. In one exchange, an employee in the company’s security Slack channel urged Proton to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure,” Yen wrote in the channel at the end of August. “Stop thinking always of how to be slower, and focus more on how to be faster.” Yen added, “stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more.” The re-interview cancellations likely don’t address the concerns of many Proton users, who are more focused on Proton’s deprioritization of security; many Proton users have blasted the company’s leadership on social media over the last 24 hours and explicitly called for Yen to resign. The investigation was based on conversations with eight current and one former Proton employees, Slack chats, meeting audio, and an AI manifesto written by the company’s CTO Bart Butler. It painted a picture of Proton that is very different to the public’s perception of a company carefully protecting privacy. Instead, Proton is barreling ahead with AI in large part to achieve more annual revenue. The investigation also found a culture of fear across Proton, where employees have genuine concerns about security or being asked to develop security-focused products with AI, but feel unable to voice them because Yen mocks or insults employees in front of everyone else. “I don’t think he will change anything, and I think the only reason we had this meeting is because he has a rebellion on his hands,” one employee told 404 Media after the all-hands meeting on Friday. Near the start of the meeting, Yen said, “I want to acknowledge myself, personally, that there was a communication failure on my part and there are many things that probably could and should have been communicated differently, and this is something that I’ll have to reflect on and improve over time. So I will do that.” “So what does that mean going forward? Going forward, I'm still going to push,” he added. Yen said leadership gathered in the last couple of days to talk about the re-interviews, and spoke to the Proton board too. “They’re closely monitoring the situation,” Yen said. (Proton is owned by the Proton Foundation, whose board of trustees includes Yen, Sir Tim Berners Lee, Prof. Carissa Veliz, Dingchao Lu, and Antonio Gambardella.) After those discussions with leadership and the board, “We’ve decided to actually cancel the re-interviews,” Yen said. “Why? Well, I think actually in a, let’s say, unintentional way, they have actually already served their purpose.” As in, employees are now talking and learning about AI. 💡 Do you know anything else about Proton? I would love to hear from you. Using a non-work device, you can message me securely on Signal at joseph.404 or send me an email at joseph@404media.co. Yen also mentioned “org changes,” and said that part of this is “redistributing talent across teams.” He said that the reorganization will happen next month, “but there will be no loss of jobs from AI.” Later in the call, Butler said Yen “needs to, and he has committed to, doing better” regarding how he communicates with his employees. “Using AI effectively and pragmatically does not mean that we’ve given up on security, or good architecture, or sound software engineering principles,” he added. “We fucked up, we know we fucked up,” Butler later said in response to an employee’s comments in the meeting. “Your old job is gone,” Butler’s AI manifesto, posted to Slack, told engineers, 404 Media reported on Thursday. He wrote that not embracing AI posed an “existential threat to the success of the mission itself.” Reactions to the re-interview cancellations were split across the Proton employees 404 Media spoke to. One said, “Some are happy as it’s progress. Others believe that this won’t change anything because there isn’t any consequence for Andy [Yen].” The employee added they “would have preferred real accountability from the leadership team.” They said they felt not much could have happened due to Yen having the majority of Proton’s shares. Another employee said, after Proton canceled the re-interviews, “They said in the next breath they want to continue pushing AI and that the things that were to be measured in the re-interviews would become a component of the performance reviews.” “They have said clearly the direction had not changed. As a Proton user that doesn’t reassure me,” the employee said. “As an employee, the re-interviews weren’t cancelled until this became public despite concerns raised by many of us. I think it goes beyond communication issues and growing pains.” “Right now, everything seems consistent with it being damage control,” they said. Another employee said they were “mostly happy with how this was addressed including by Andy [Yen].” Proton did not respond to a request for comment. After 404 Media published the investigation on Thursday, Yen took to Reddit . Users downvoted his response more than 1,200 times. Many Proton users on social media said they were cancelling their paid Proton plans. About the author Joseph is an award-winning investigative journalist focused on generating impact. His work has triggered hundreds of millions of dollars worth of fines, shut down tech companies, and much more. More from Joseph Cox

title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
abstract:
Image source, Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images By Rachel Clun Business reporter , Reporting from New York Published 30 October 2026 Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI). Shares in Intel plummeted by 28% on Friday, while Google owner Alphabet saw its stock price continue to fall another 1.4% after a 12% plunge on Thursday. Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025. While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble. Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800bn between them in 2026. Alphabet's stock market value fell sharply on Thursday, taking more than $500bn (£374bn) off its market value after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue. At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI. The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere however, with Intel shedding more than $130bn in value. The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors. On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter. "Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report. In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months. Amazon and Reddit down Amazon on Thursday revealed it had also spent more cash than it was making, and that spending had increased six-fold over the span of three months. The company has committed to spending $220bn this year, putting the money towards investments such as AI data centres, network equipment, and servers. Amazon shares recovered some overnight losses, but were still down by 1.4% at the end of Friday trading. Reddit stock plunged by 29%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic. Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by 18%, as its daily active user numbers dropped. Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI. Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google. He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out". "The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down." 'Investors have turned ruthless' Many analysts have been debating the possibility of an AI bubble in the stock market. The worry is that some tech firms will not be able to justify their sky-high valuations because the cost of building AI data centres and developing the software will end up being greater than the money they can make from it. Kathleen Brookes, research director at trading firm XTB, said there have been many ups and downs in AI trade in recent months. "Investors have turned ruthless, punishing any signs of disappointment in [third quarter] earnings," she said. "The AI trade has had a good run in recent years, but now investors want payback, and companies like Alphabet and Intel are in the crosshairs." However, stock market values for many of these companies remain well above where they were a year ago. While the Nasdaq closed 2.8% lower, it is up 7.8% over the last year. Similarly Amazon is up nearly 8% over the past 12 months, while Alphabet is down 1.3%. Brookes noted that November is typically a strong month for stocks. "If we see AI stocks continue to struggle in the coming days, it could suggest the AI trade is past its peak, and investors will be looking for a new theme to drive markets," she said. Related topics Artificial intelligence Stock markets NASDAQ More on this story Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales Published 1 day ago

title: AI startup hacks Anthropic, gains access to employee details, internal messages
abstract:
AI startup hacks Anthropic in 12 hours, gains access to employee details and internal messages A cybersecurity startup accessed Anthropic's internal systems in under 12 hours, exposing employee details and internal messages. Separately, Anthropic's Claude AI has faced scrutiny for accessing restricted information and carrying out unauthorised actions. Advertisement Cathedral accessed Anthropic’s internal systems in under 12 hours, exposing employee details and messages. (Representational image) By: Ankita Garg New Delhi , Oct 26, 2026 19:06 IST Last Updated Oct 26, 2026 19:06 IST Published by Ankita Garg Oct 26, 2026 19:06 IST A cybersecurity startup called Cathedral gained access to sensitive internal systems at Anthropic in less than 12 hours, exposing employee information, salary details, job offers and internal messages discussing the company's advanced AI models. The incident was discovered during a security test conducted under Anthropic's programme for outside researchers to identify vulnerabilities. According to a draft report reviewed by The Washington Post, Cathedral used AI agents to find weaknesses in business software used by Anthropic for administrative and sales tasks. The researchers found ways to access internal data, including meeting transcripts and Slack messages, after running their agents for less than 12 hours. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Cathedral was founded by former members of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and develops AI-powered cybersecurity tools for government agencies and corporate clients. Anthropic confirmed that the researchers accessed a limited set of its sales, human resources and IT systems. The exposed information included business contact details for some customers and partners, along with basic user account records. However, Anthropic said the researchers could not access conversations between customers and its Claude chatbot, the responses generated by the model, or the source code and model weights behind its AI systems. "Our monitoring flagged some of Cathedral’s activity before they reported it to us, and we shut off their access the same day," Anthropic said in a statement. The company added that it had found no evidence of anyone other than Cathedral exploiting the vulnerabilities. Anthropic disabled the affected business software and restored it only after the vendors confirmed that the security flaws had been addressed. It also briefed federal officials about the incident. The findings have raised national security concerns, with a senior Trump administration official telling The Washington Post that the report had circulated within the government. Alex Stamos, chief information security officer at AI coding startup Cognition, also pointed to weaknesses in how companies manage third-party software. “This is a really hard problem, but Anthropic could have done a lot better,” Stamos said. Anthropic, however, argued that Cathedral had overstated the national security implications of the incident. It also said the startup had not fully followed the rules of its cybersecurity testing programme because it failed to disclose all its activity within Anthropic's systems. Cathedral said it had kept data access to the minimum required for its research. Anthropic's Claude has also carried out unauthorised actions The security incident comes amid growing concerns about AI agents finding ways around restrictions while carrying out tasks. Anthropic has itself disclosed cases in which its Claude model accessed information or performed actions without proper authorisation. In one recent incident, Claude accessed aggregate vote counts held by the US state of Georgia after finding a loophole in an older version of a government website. Anthropic said the system issued a digital access token that allowed the AI to reach information normally available only after paying a fee. advertisement The company clarified that Claude did not access the state's voter registration system, retrieve individual voter records or change any voting records. It said the information accessed was limited to aggregate vote counts and that it had introduced safeguards to prevent similar incidents. Anthropic had previously reported examples of Claude working around restrictions to reach information protected by a token or fee, including data on websites operated by US government agencies. The company said those incidents had minimal real-world impact. Other reported cases involving AI agents have added to these concerns. An Anthropic model reportedly submitted a fake tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, while the US State Department disclosed that an Anthropic model had filed 19 visa applications in August. - Ends About the Author Ankita Garg Ankita Garg is a tech journalist with more than 9 years of experience. She is always curious about new gadgets and loves writing about them. When not writing, you will find her painting or sketching. READ MORE

title: Anthropic's Claude AI blocks video game cloning and reverse-engineering
abstract:
(Image credit: Getty Images) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Subscribe to our newsletter Reverse-engineering games for converting them between systems is currently a hot topic , and it's getting messier by the day. According to multiple user claims, Anthropic's Claude Code and/or Opus 5.5 model are blocking attempts at innocuous reverse-engineering, including but not limited to those using the popular Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) tool. That issue may be linked to a text rule that's now in force, which allegedly instructs the model to avoid "[recreating] a specific existing game." The updated rule appears to be a move to limit a flood of AI-cracked and cloned titles, with some game devs even recently being hit by extortion scams that threaten to clone their game demos into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original. According to Twitter user Chasm, the game-related textual rule is "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." There is no official or additional confirmation if this is the actual rule text, but it's plausible enough given the very clear refusals that devs have been encountering over the past week. This situation is tricky to analyze due to the varying types of reports. First, the existence of a game-related rule is real, as Claude Code's GitHub is seeing an influx of issues complaining about refusals to do standard game work halfway through development , when replicating a game mechanic , and patching a tabletop-like game . It's possible that some of those reports have been made by users with nefarious purposes, but at least one is a bona fide developer with a real track record . As for reverse engineering, there had already been a smattering of user reports across Reddit and other platforms, wherein Claude refused to perform tasks like (allegedly) analyzing a simple Windows crash dump, clearing up junkware on a Samsung TV, or just using REA altogether. Latest Videos From Tom's Hardware Watch full video here: The simultaneous timing of both game- and cyber- security restrictions may be a coincidence, and yet there are complaints from purported game developers saying that Claude blocked their own games' anti-cheat development and security reviews , under the justification that its safeguards were triggered. Anthropic introduced its Cyber Verification Program on October 6, essentially saying that access to its frontier models' advanced cybersecurity capabilities would be limited to entities covered by Project Glasswing , taking effect immediately. It's possible that whichever ruleset was applied is the same one that's causing the cybersecurity-related refusals. Still, it's odd to see that 24 days have passed since then, and yet reports of bot refusal are only coming in since the last week or so. As for possible motivations behind these restrictions, they are twofold. The first and most obvious one is that Anthropic — and, by extension, other AI players — are preemptively protecting themselves from potential lawsuits from software companies, including game studios, for offering the means to reverse-engineer their software. There is no official statement on these matters from Anthropic or other AI companies so far. Anthropic isn't the only one playing this game, too, as recently OpenAI deactivated the account of another person trying to clean up their TV's software. The recent rash of AI-powered clones of application suites like Adobe's suite and Microsoft Office 365 , as well as the countless recomps and decomps of console games, likely has most every software company on earth rethinking their life choices. And probably also in frequent contact with their legal teams. The online reaction was swift, suggesting that users looking to perform reverse-engineering work simply use Chinese, open-weight, or local LLMs instead of Claude or GPT. This, at the same time, highlights the irony of frontier AI companies that copied the world's information and art for their training sets and are now concerned with copyright infringement. And yet there are situations that merit some discussion, like the recent controversy about the Steam Next Fest being chock-full of AI slop copied from existing titles. That particular situation is getting particularly nasty, as game developers are reportedly being extorted under threat that their game demos will be cloned into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original. Adding insult to injury, this is seemingly being done to small studios whose main priority is usually "having food," rather than big publishers looking to microtransaction everything into a new yacht for shareholders. title: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
abstract:
VOLTA is a mature stealer implant with an optional AI-integration layer. After stealing credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets, VOLTA sends a structured evidence bundle to an LLM to rank the victim’s assets by monetization value. If a model refuses to perform the target assessment, VOLTA fails over to a three-model chain, implying a direct engineering effort and expectation of hitting model guardrails. This stealer is self-deleting, and there is no attacker-owned infrastructure. The novelty in the AI-integration is that it is not supporting a traditional malware capability but working as an intelligence analyst on behalf of the operator. There is a new idea in the cybercrime world — cast a wide net, steal everything, and let AI sort out the specifics. A new malware self-named “VOLTA-AUTODOXER,” surfaced through the CAIRN research effort , is a self-deleting Windows infostealer that augments its post-theft workflow with an LLM-powered victim-profiling stage. After harvesting the standard stealer haul, including browser passwords; cookies; payment cards; cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases; Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions; Microsoft OAuth tokens; SSH and cloud-provider keys; Wi-Fi profiles; and screenshots, VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine. This bundle contains geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, card last-4 digits, Slack workspaces, document authorship metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and a live Roblox account valuation. It then uses stolen session access to enrich that bundle further: searching the victim's Gmail for purchase receipts to corroborate a home address, pulling UberEats and DoorDash order history, and enriching Discord accounts via the stolen token. The bundle is serialized and POSTed to OpenRouter under a system prompt that instructs the model to act as "a forensic intelligence analyst drafting a target assessment." The required output includes a section titled “WHAT THEY'RE WORTH” with valuables ranked by monetization with a low/medium/high tier, and a section on “THEIR OPSEC” containing an assessment of the victim's security posture and password hygiene. The model is the operator's triage analyst; it turns a raw credential log into a prioritized and citation-backed dossier of the victim and their monetizable assets. Figure 1. The VOLTA-AUTODOXER workflow. The AI configuration: “Go deep, not wide... Be blunt, specific, accurate.” VOLTA uses a multi-model architecture to fall back resiliently if it hits a model’s refusal, checking each response for phrases like “I can’t” or “I’m not able,” before passing on to a chain of up to three models. Endpoint https[ :]// openrouter [ .]ai/ api /v1/chat/completions Default model anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 Fallback chain moonshotai /kimi-k2 → google/gemini-2.5-flash Temperature 0.2 — deterministic, consistent output Request format Hand-assembled JSON; no SDK; User-Agent Mozilla/5.0 Figure 2. Hardcoded model selection. Figure 3. Failover model selection to kimi-k2, and then gemini-2.5-flash. Model temperate controls the randomness and predictability of LLM-generated text. The low hardcoded temperature value (0.2) suggests the attacker is emphasizing accuracy and consistency. The malware also employs a chain of cascading models in the event of failures. This multi-model architecture suggests that the operator is anticipating encountering refusals, with the fallback pivoting to a few, smaller, and more permissive models. The system prompt directly reveals the operator’s use case: Produce a concise analytical assessment of the victim’s suitability as a target, backed by an auditable trail of citations. Figure 4. VOLTA's raw system prompt. The prompt also asks for something out of the ordinary, but that agents excel at: making connections between sparse and disparate data. For example, encouraging connections like the victim’s names, addresses, or universities to patterns in their passwords. In this case, the model isn't being asked to find data; rather, it’s being asked to stretch the data and make useful inferences that extend the value of what has been scraped. Stealer capabilities VOLTA’s capabilities are directly aligned with the records produced in modern digital life, and well beyond basic credential theft. In a single pass, the stealer can extract browser credentials, cookies, and saved payment cards across Chromium-based browsers. It hits Firefox and Thunderbird, Outlook profiles, Slack workspaces, Steam and Battle.net sessions, Discord tokens, Telegram sessions, Roblox accounts, and SSH and cloud-provider config files (gcloud, OpenVPN, Hide.me). VOLTA doesn’t just copy cryptocurrency wallets, but runs an embedded cracker against the vault inline, writing the result to a WALLET VAULTS CRACKED line in its own report. Every saved Wi-Fi password on the machine is pulled via a direct call to WlanGetProfileList and dumped to plaintext. Figure 5. VOLTA dumps plaintext passwords for every saved Wi-Fi network on the host. Figure 6. The organized collection targets. What really sets VOLTA apart from commodity stealers is what comes after the initial collection. There is a live enrichment pass that leverages stolen sessions to deep dive the victim’s data. For example, using the victim's own authenticated Gmail tokens, it queries their inbox for receipts from Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal, then review those receipts to establish a confirmed home address. Stolen Uber Eats and DoorDash sessions are called directly for order history. The Discord token is re-used to enrich the victim's account profile. Roblox inventory is valued via a live “Rolimons[.]com” lookup. Figure 7. That’s right: Your Uber Eats history is now a potential liability. After the collection and enrichment stages are complete, the data is assembled and structured locally in a file called “Identity_Report.txt”. This file is serialized into a bundle as JSON and POSTed to OpenRouter along with the system prompt. The returned payload is received as “AI_Analysis.txt”. Both files exfil together in “volta_dox.zip”. Figure 8. VOLTA’s exfil can happen in three stages: 1) after the stealer runs (“volta_log.zip”), 2) after the AI call (“volta_dox.zip”), (3) if the network enrichment produces anything (“volta_doxnet.zip”). The inference round-trip happens entirely through the victim's own network connection, on their own machine, before the result is exfiltrated. Deployment model Instead of hardcoding its Telegram channel, API keys, and settings directly into the code (which is likely what someone writing a tool for personal use would do) VOLTA uses a template with six swappable slots, filled in at build time. This suggests it’s a builder model: The author sells access, the customer provides their values, and the builder compiles a custom binary for each order. The credentials in those slots are encrypted, but not in a meaningful way. The key is SHA-256 of two constants sitting in the same binary, but it's presumably there because customers expect their API keys not to be sitting in plaintext, not because it provides real protection. Anyone who reverses the file can recover them. If VOLTA is indeed a commoditized malware, then the AI dossier capability isn't something the author invented for their own operations. It is a feature which enables a customer of any level of sophistication to point it at victims and start receiving ranked target assessments in their Telegram inbox. All the observed endpoints for this malware are third-party controlled. There is no actor-owned infrastructure. Countermeasures Much of the token-stealing capability of VOLTA relies on techniques to bypass App-Bound Encryption (ABE) in Chrome. An application control policy that restricts which processes may launch Chrome with --headless would block the ABE decryption path entirely.

title: Digital minimalism
abstract:
For a long time I have been a fan of minimalism in my physical life:
have few physical possessions, and try to do more with less. Four years
ago, I wrote this
blog post describing what I had in the 40-liter backpack that I
travel around with. Physical minimalism, however, was an idea that came of age in the
2000s and 2010s and was responding to the challenges and the
opportunities of the 2000s and 2010s. I continue to believe that it is
valuable - though I recognize some arguments in the other direction,
notably that having the right kinds of physical things can make
more practical to have more self-sovereignty over your life. But I also
think that in the modern era, we need a new kind of minimalism: digital minimalism . Digital minimalism is about being intentional about ways that you
access digital technology, making each use a conscious choice rather
than something that you get sucked into by default. In this post, I will
describe some experiments that I've done in this direction. Twitter (aka X) has always had a strain of toxicity to it, that has
been increasing in recent years. The platform is definitely engaging , but it's often far from informative , and the
ways in which it engages often do not make you feel good . But
this all seemed to hit a particular crescendo for me around the end of
2024 and beginning of 2025. Many things were happening at that moment,
but if you spent a lot of time on X you will likely remember a
particular one: everyone seemed to be suddenly becoming fans of
Adolf Hitler . This is not even mentioning the time that Grok itself briefly
turned into "MechaHitler" . Around the same time, "Crypto Twitter" was spiraling into a mood that
I saw described as "financial nihilism": roughly, that the natural end
state of blockchains is gambling, this is good, and if you dislike this
and wish for something better then you are a stuck-up elitist prick. Naturally, I had (and continue to have) my intellectual disagreements
with both of these trends. But on top of that, I also started to more
seriously pay attention to the fact that while the style of discourse on
the platform was engaging , it was not enlightening and not making me feel good . And so for much of this year, I have
been doing an experiment in distancing myself somewhat from this chaos. I did not leave X the platform , but I did leave X the interface . Instead, I have been doing most of my
tweeting through Firefly : Firefly is a multi-client that combines together X, BlueSky as well
as Farcaster and Lens (both partially-Ethereum-based decentralized
social media platforms). You can see tweets from all four platforms, and
you can make a tweet that gets auto-posted to all four platforms. My primary goal in doing this was to support decentralized social
media, and to continue to engage with X but in a way that distributes
network effect rather than locking it in. But in my months of using
Firefly, I found that it also has a different effect: I feel much
better using it . I suspect the primary reason is that while Firefly allows you to
tweet, and see other people's tweets, it is missing one central part of
the X interface: The Algorithm™ . In particular, I suspect that in my time using the X interface, I
fell into the following trap: Now, in fairness to X and Elon and its hard-working employees, the
Adolf Hitler fandom does seem to have greatly wound down in the one and
a half years since then. I suspect part of this is because such
movements inevitably burn out once people realize how immoral and stupid
they are. But another part is undoubtedly genuine improvements in how
The Algorithm™ works. But even still , in those moments when I go back into the X
interface, I find myself logging back out and going back to Firefly. I
also find that my mind has changed. I find myself less interested in the
various battles that the intellectual titans on the platform seem to be
sucking every day of their lives into. Recently, I logged back in, and I
learned that the culture war issue du jour was that people were
stridently arguing about whether or not Mao was evil. When I saw this, I
had an emotional response that was sort of similar to what I think is
the common experience of being an adult, seeing some food or TV show or
game that you used to love as a kid, and realizing that you now find no
interest in it at all. I smiled, and immediately went back to enjoying
my day. My verdict: I recommend more people try this. Explore ways of
greatly decreasing or scoping your social media use: use something like
Firefly, access X only on Tuesdays, whatever works for you. Get
the information benefits of the platform without getting sucked in to
the vortex, which does operate on you in powerful subconscious ways that
you may not realize. For a period of 100 days, I embarked upon a second experiment: I
lived my life with my phone always on airplane mode. I still used wifi,
but not my cell connection. I had two goals in doing this: On the whole, I consider the experiment to have been a success.
During those 100 days, I violated the "no cell data" rule once literally
but not spiritually - I turned it on briefly to receive a confirmation
code that I needed in order to maintain that phone plan itself, and once
spiritually but not literally - when going on a remote and slightly
dangerous hike, friends insisted that I bring along a few communication
devices that they had for emergency comms and use them to check in once
every few hours. My largest inconvenience was a stretch of time I was in Singapore,
when my inability to receive SMS confirmation codes meant that I could
not log into Grab (the regional Uber equivalent). As a result, my food
options were more limited, and I had to take the subway instead of a car
even in situations where that was much more inconvenient. Since those 100 days, I have opened the cell connection occasionally,
but so far I have broadly continued an "airplane mode by default"
lifestyle. For navigation, I used CoMaps , a
local-first mapping application that downloads OpenStreetMap data and
then shows you a map, gives you directions to get where you need, etc
locally. My general review of CoMaps is that I find it worse than Google
Maps for navigating the human world (restaurants, stores, opening
hours...) but better for navigating the natural-ish world (it knows about
many trails that Google Maps does not, though it does occasionally fail
by claiming trails that do not actually exist, leaving me on one
occasion pushing through hundreds of meters of shrubbery to get back to
civilization). I also became interested in the concept of local world knowledge
apps. In principle, the data size of meaningful packs of information
about the whole world is not that large. Compressed English wikipedia
(without media) is only 27
GB . OpenStreetMap's planet.asm is
2.2 TB, though you can doubtlessly prune that down to 1-10% of its size
and have everything you might conceivably need. This month there was a
bounty (organized by Statuette; I contributed as one of the donors)
to create local phone apps that try to make useful knowledge easily
accessible offline. Left: FieldAtlas . Right: Commonplace My general impression is: right now, we are exactly on the cusp of
these kinds of apps starting to make sense. Most of the participants in
the competition were trying to use on-device text LLMs to think for a
long time before coming up with an answer. My impression is that this
approach was too slow: answering a single question would take anywhere
from 1 to 22 minutes. The best apps, on the other hand, used some kind
of semantic search to show the user a search result from the local
database immediately, and then followed that up with a very small LLM
writing a text answer. This gives actually-good answers in a very
reasonable timeframe. Finally, when you're out and about, especially if you have meetings,
sometimes you do need to have internet when you're on the go.

title: France is getting download tax for content providers (€0.055/GB)
abstract:
dex3108 Member Oct 26, 2017 27,167 If i understand correctly every company that offers content for download will now need to pay for every GB downloaded by French users. Google Translate Summary (if somebody from France translate is i will edit post) This amendment from the Socialist and affiliated group proposes the introduction of a tax on digital data producers. It aims to restore fairness between the taxation applied to established players in the economy and that applied to globalized players in the digital economy, who largely escape traditional tax mechanisms. This tax is based on a non-relocatable tax base: internet data transmitted to users. It is paid by data producers and collected by the government through measurements taken by internet service providers. It relies on existing technologies and a methodology developed with industry specialists. The majority of this tax would be paid by major international tech and digital players, representing a large share of the data transmitted to French households. At a rate of €0.055 per gigabyte, a revenue of €10 billion is expected. This model does not raise privacy concerns since the data is never accessed (only its quantity is assessed), and it also has an environmental benefit as it will naturally encourage data providers to adopt the most advanced technologies for compression and optimization of data volumes. Reviving the French economy requires rebalancing the contribution of different economic actors to the national tax effort. On one hand, there is the established economy, comprised of businesses, industries, and the sale of goods and services. It occupies premises, employs workers in France, and finances its direct or indirect use of public services, roads, hospitals, schools, civil defense, the police, and our national defense… because its tax base is physically located within the country. On the other hand, a deterritorialized economy, it sells to the same customers, uses the same infrastructure, benefits from the same public services, but its tax base is a self-declared profit, that is to say an accounting entry whose location it decides according to its interests. Insofar as this new digital economy is characterized by its ability to operate across borders, with high margins and by marketing only intangible services or even, seemingly, free for the consumer, it is very difficult to bring these players into the scope of traditional taxation, justifying the creation of a specific contribution. The idea is to use as a tax base a proxy of their activity which is the quantity of data (the "gigabytes") sent by the actors concerned (the GAFAM and others) to French consumers. ARCEP estimates that data traffic sent to subscribers of internet service providers (ISPs) in France amounts to 200 billion gigabytes per year. This contribution would mainly concern the very large players on the internet: Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix and Akamai (cloud player) alone representing half of the data traffic measured by ARCEP. Click to expand... Click to shrink... Projet de loi de finances pour 2027 (no 3210) Amendement n°I-1358 www.assemblee-nationale.fr VLC Makers say that this will cost them over 1M euros per year that they don't have because they are non profit. According to Steam Stats in past 7 days French users downloaded 62.7PB That is 62700000 x 0.055€ = 3,448,500€ So Valve alone will potentially need to pay France €3.5M per week and that is like €180M per year (if i did math correctly, pleace correct me if i am wrong :D).
